first_reader_check.about: Whether a pass on a tagged assessment item (a standard code, a cognitive domain, a rubric criterion) requires the tagged competency, tested without student data by searching for assessment bypasses: solvers that lack the competency by an explicit restriction on their operations or their information, never see the key, and pass under the published scoring rule. The method is general; it is run on public-release mathematics items, where tags, keys, and scoring rules are public.
first_reader_check.shown: Under a pre-registered bar, language models of two families recover New York Regents Algebra I and II keys with every given quantity withheld, and the recovery survives a form-preserving change of every option value; on those items a pass does not require computing on the givens, so the key does not carry the evidence it is read as, and whether it requires the tagged operation is left open. Small programs denied the tagged operation match keys on a few cells. TIMSS cognitive-domain cells yield no bypass at public sizes. Rates are claimed on items re-read from the printed page, which released text layers often misstate.
first_reader_check.what_is_new: The assessment bypass as a one-sided, student-free, executable test of any tag, with two domain-neutral restriction kinds (capability and information); a pre-registered witness bar with hashed programs and Holm correction inside each solver family; the first instantiation on 2,405 tagged public-release mathematics items; and the measurement finding that the released text layer must be replaced by a page re-read before any rate is claimed.
first_reader_check.why_a_big_deal: Accountability, procurement, and research read a tagged pass as evidence of the tagged competency in every subject. The abstract says the reading assumes passing requires the competency, that the search refutes that requirement without students wherever tags, item text, keys, and an executable scoring rule are public, and that on the Regents algebra cells the key does not carry the evidence it is read as. The last sentence states the scope plainly: a method demonstration on one subject.
abstract_says: first paragraph: tags in general (standard codes, cognitive domains, rubric criteria); the reading of a pass as evidence in accountability, procurement, and research; the assumption; the bypass as the test, glossed inline; one-sided in one sentence

second paragraph: instantiation on public-release mathematics items where tags, keys, and scoring rules are public, under a pre-registered bar; Algebra I and II language-model bypass in two model families surviving the form-preserving option-value change; the consequence for the key as evidence; the tagged-operation question left open; small programs on a few cells; TIMSS null at public sizes; rates claimed on the printed page; scope sentence: a method demonstration on one subject, and what the search needs elsewhere
few numbers: none beyond the two cell names and the two model families
first_reader_check.no_conjunction_contradicted_by_a_table: The abstract conjoins Algebra I and II recovery with survival under the option-value change; Table tab:isomorph shows every scorer clearing on both cells under the rank-preserving arm on the repaired-verified population. The new cross-family column of Table tab:repaired is a stricter sensitivity, not the claim population; its one miss (Phi-4 Algebra II, dagger) is stated in Results 4.2 and does not contradict an abstract sentence, which speaks of the claim population and of two families, both of which still clear Algebra II there (Qwen2.5 7B and 14B, Phi-4).
first_reader_check.intro_lead: Paragraph 1: an assessment item carries a tag that names the competency it is said to measure; a correct answer is read as evidence of that competency in accountability, procurement, and research; each use assumes passing requires the competency; testing standards and validity theory. Paragraph 2: the bypass, its two restriction kinds with one non-mathematics example each (lexical policy on a causal-inference item; passage-withheld reader on a reading-comprehension item, cited to partial-input baselines), one-sidedness, and where the requirement question sits relative to alignment tools and psychometrics. Paragraph 3: mathematics first, and why, in one sentence; then the findings. Contribution lead-in says the object and bar are general and the census and findings are the mathematics instantiation; bullet 3 opens with 'The first instantiation of the method'.

first_reader_check.body_first_reader: Method 3.1 defines bypass and both restriction kinds without a subject; Method 3.2 is where mathematics enters. Method 3.6 names the cross-family verified population in one sentence and assigns the roles (claim: repaired-verified; stricter sensitivity: cross-family; looser: repaired all; audit trail: text layer and filter). Results 4.1 gives its counts, Table 1 shows it as the first column with the claimed column labelled, and Results 4.2 states plainly which rows hold on it and that Phi-4 Algebra II does not. Related Work's collective-advance paragraph states the object as general with the mathematics census as its first instantiation. Limitations list ten weaknesses (page instrument with what the second family settles and what remains; language-model coders; template memorization; 14B floor with its cause; one-rater sheet; small unreplicated catalog rows; STAAR replication forms and parse; instruction-only not run; constructed response; ingestion). The Conclusion carries what the method needs to run on another domain, once.
